me - ⟦name|Callum Fairweather-Ngata⟧
old flat - ⟦street address|Flat 2B, 41 Ecclesall Grove, Sheffield S11 8QT⟧
landlord - ⟦name|Desmond Pryce-Whitlock⟧ (manages it himself, no agent)
moved out 31 aug, deposit £1,150 protected with the DPS, deposit ID 2087-4412-9930
he wants to keep £340 for "professional carpet clean" but the check-out report from 1 sept literally says carpets "good, light wear"
new address - ⟦street address|112 Abbeydale Road South, Sheffield S7 2QL⟧
my email for the letter - ⟦email address|c.fairweather.ngata@gmail.com⟧

he only ever answers texts (⟦phone number|07700 914362⟧) and he's got an email ⟦email address|desmond.pw@btinternet.com⟧ he never checks, but i want a proper paper letter this time so theres a record.

i read on martin lewis's site that the DPS has a free dispute thing so maybe mention that? and if he just wants to pay me directly it's lloyds ⟦account number|30-96-17 51849302⟧

Assistant: Of course. Here's a draft you can post (ideally with proof of postage from the Post Office) and also attach to an email, so there's a dated copy either way. It sets a clear deadline and mentions the DPS dispute service as the next step rather than as a threat.

---

⟦name|Callum Fairweather-Ngata⟧
⟦street address|112 Abbeydale Road South
Sheffield
S7 2QL⟧
⟦email address|c.fairweather.ngata@gmail.com⟧

18 October 2026

Mr ⟦name|D. Pryce-Whitlock⟧
[Landlord's postal address]

Dear Mr ⟦name|Pryce-Whitlock⟧,

Re: Return of tenancy deposit – ⟦street address|Flat 2B, 41 Ecclesall Grove, Sheffield S11 8QT⟧
DPS deposit ID: 2087-4412-9930

I vacated the above property on 31 August 2026 at the end of my tenancy. Seven weeks have now passed and my deposit of £1,150 has not been returned.

You have proposed a deduction of £340 for professional carpet cleaning. The check-out report dated 1 September 2026 records the carpets as "good, light wear", which is consistent with fair wear and tear after a two-year tenancy. I do not agree to this deduction.

Please confirm release of the full deposit through the DPS within 10 working days of the date of this letter. If you would prefer to repay me directly, my bank details are:

Account name: ⟦name|C Fairweather-Ngata⟧
Sort code: ⟦account number|30-96-17⟧
Account number: ⟦account number|51849302⟧

If I have not heard from you by 1 November 2026, I will open a dispute through the DPS's free alternative dispute resolution service and submit the check-out report as evidence.

Yours sincerely,

⟦name|Callum Fairweather-Ngata⟧

---

A couple of tips:
- Keep the check-out report and any photos you took on move-out day somewhere safe.
- The DPS dispute service is free for tenants, so you don't need a solicitor for a sum like this.

Someone opened a Capital One card AND a Verizon account in my name. Credit frozen, FTC report filed. What am I missing?

Using an alt because my sister follows my main.

Last Tuesday I got a "Welcome to your new Quicksilver card!" letter from Capital One. Never applied. The letter shows the card as ⟦credit card number|XXXX XXXX XXXX 8817⟧. I pulled all three reports on annualcreditreport.com and found:

- Capital One card opened 9/22, $4,500 limit, $3,980 already spent (mostly gift cards and a Best Buy run)
- Verizon postpaid account opened 9/24 with two iPhones financed (~$2,300)
- a hard inquiry from Synchrony on 9/26 I don't recognize

The card was mailed to ⟦street address|4410 Brightwater Ln Apt 6, Mesquite, TX 75150⟧. I have never lived in Mesquite. The Capital One rep read back the SSN on the application as ⟦ssn|***-**-6093⟧ (mine) and the DOB as ⟦date of birth|04/17/1991⟧ (also mine), and the Verizon fraud team said the application had my TX driver license number, ⟦driver license number|31847726⟧, so whoever did this had my actual documents, not just a data-breach dump.

I'm about 80% sure who it is. My ex-roommate ⟦name|Tavish Coyle⟧ had access to my filing cabinet when we shared a duplex in Garland, and he moved out in August owing me two months of rent. The contact number on the Verizon account is ⟦phone number|469-724-0182⟧, which was his Google Voice number when we lived together.

What I've done so far:
1. Froze credit at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion (and saved the PINs)
2. FTC report at IdentityTheft.gov, report #178334920
3. Police report with Garland PD, case 26-041177
4. Called Capital One fraud, card closed, dispute ref CO-77120-QX
5. Verizon says the account is "under fraud review" and to call back in 5–7 business days

My coworker ⟦name|Yusuf al-Khatib⟧ went through this in 2022 and said to also get an IRS IP PIN and check ChexSystems. Anything else? I keep thinking about that Frank Abagnale movie, except it's way less fun when it's your credit score.

EDIT: Yes, I've changed the locks. Yes, I know I should have shredded stuff.
EDIT 2: ⟦name|Tavish⟧, if you're reading this, the detective already has the screenshots.

We stayed four nights in the Garden Suite (room 7) for our 15th anniversary. The breakfast alone is worth it: shakshuka, proper filter coffee, and koeksisters on the Sunday. Our host ⟦name|Thandeka⟧ remembered that I'd mentioned the anniversary in an email and left a bottle of Hamilton Russell pinot noir in the room with a card. My husband ⟦name|Pieter⟧ stood up on his third wave and has not stopped talking about it.

The hiccup: Booking.com had our reservation (confirmation 4417.208.356) down as three nights instead of four, and on night four the room was booked to another couple. ⟦name|Thandeka⟧ sorted it out within twenty minutes and moved them to the Fig Room, which turned out fine (we ended up sharing a braai with them, ⟦name|Joost⟧ and ⟦name|Anneke van der Velde⟧ from Utrecht, and now we're Facebook friends) but it was stressful for a moment.

Value: R2,350 per night including breakfast. Would absolutely go back. Ask for a room facing Boyes Drive if you want the mountain view.

Assistant: Two separate problems here, ⟦name|Paweł⟧: the crash, and the matching logic.

**1. The crash**

Row ⟦customer id|C-0051207⟧ (⟦name|Józef Bąk⟧) has an empty email. Even with `dtype=str`, pandas reads empty cells as `NaN`, which is a float, so `e.strip()` fails. Use the vectorised string methods, which pass NaN through instead of crashing:

```python
df["email_norm"] = df["email"].str.strip().str.lower()
```

**2. The matching**

Right now you dedupe on first + last name only. That's why the two ⟦name|Marek Zieliński⟧ rows collapse into one, while "⟦name|Wróblewska⟧" and "⟦name|WROBLEWSKA⟧" never match (`.lower()` fixes the case, but `ó` is still not `o`). A sturdier rule: two rows are the same customer only if the normalised name matches *and* at least one contact detail matches.

```python
import re
from itertools import combinations

import pandas as pd
from unidecode import unidecode

SRC = r"C:\Users\⟦username|pkowalczyk⟧\Downloads\customers_export_2026-10-17.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(SRC, dtype=str)
df["orders"] = df["orders"].astype(int)

def norm_text(s):
    return "" if pd.isna(s) else unidecode(s).strip().lower()

def norm_phone(p):
    if pd.isna(p):
        return ""
    return re.sub(r"\D", "", p)[-9:]      # Polish numbers: last 9 digits, drops +48

def norm_street(a):
    a = norm_text(a)
    a = re.sub(r"^(ul|al|pl)\.\s*", "", a)
    a = re.sub(r"\s+m\.\s*", "/", a)      # "14 m. 3" -> "14/3"
    return a.split(",")[0].replace(" ", "")

df["name_key"] = df["first_name"].map(norm_text) + "|" + df["last_name"].map(norm_text)
df["email_key"] = df["email"].map(norm_text)
df["phone_key"] = df["phone"].map(norm_phone)
df["street_key"] = df["address"].map(norm_street)

parent = list(range(len(df)))
def find(i):
    while parent[i] != i:
        parent[i] = parent[parent[i]]
        i = parent[i]
    return i

for i, j in combinations(range(len(df)), 2):
    a, b = df.iloc[i], df.iloc[j]
    if a["name_key"] != b["name_key"]:
        continue
    if any(a[k] and a[k] == b[k] for k in ("email_key", "phone_key", "street_key")):
        parent[find(j)] = find(i)

df["group"] = [find(i) for i in range(len(df))]
clean = df.sort_values("orders", ascending=False).drop_duplicates("group")
```

Bought this to replace a 12-year-old Panasonic that finally gave up. Paid £119.99 in the September sale (RRP £159.99). Arrived next day via DPD, tracking JD00 0224 8177 3099 15.

- The paddle started squeaking after about three weeks.

Tips for anyone new to it:
- I use the ratios from Paul Hollywood's white bloomer (500 g strong flour, 7 g yeast, 10 g salt, 320 ml water) and it fits the 1 kg setting perfectly.
- For the gluten-free programme, Doves Farm flour works; supermarket own-brand came out like a brick.
- The serial number (HB750-2209-UK-004471 on mine) is under the base. You need it to register the 3-year warranty at hearthwell.co.uk/register.

Would be 5 stars if the manual had been written by someone who has ever made bread. Mary Berry would weep.

"Juan throws a ball straight up from the edge of a rooftop 15 m above the ground with an initial velocity of 12 m/s. Maria is standing on the ground 20 m from the base of the building. Assistant: Good news first: you don't need Maria at all. The 20 m is a distractor. The ball goes straight up and comes straight down, so the horizontal distance never enters the problem.

Take "up" as positive and the ground as y = 0. The ball starts at y₀ = 15 m with v₀ = +12 m/s, and a = −9.8 m/s²:

y(t) = 15 + 12t − 4.9t²

**(a) Time to hit the ground.** Set y = 0:

4.9t² − 12t − 15 = 0

t = [12 + √(12² + 4 · 4.9 · 15)] / (2 · 4.9)
  = [12 + √(144 + 294)] / 9.8
  = (12 + 20.93) / 9.8
  ≈ **3.36 s**

(The other root is negative, so we discard it.)

**(b) Maximum height.** At the top, v = 0. Height gained above the roof: h = v₀² / 2g = 144 / 19.6 ≈ 7.35 m. So the maximum height above the ground is 15 + 7.35 ≈ **22.3 m**.

Why your answers came out different:
- **3.31 s**: this is what you get with g = 10 m/s². The problem says 9.8, so use 9.8.
- **2.97 s**: this looks like time to the top (12 / 9.8 ≈ 1.22 s) plus the time to fall 15 m (≈ 1.75 s). But from the top, the ball falls 22.3 m, not 15 m: √(2 · 22.35 / 9.8) ≈ 2.14 s, and 1.22 + 2.14 ≈ 3.36 s. Same answer as above, which is a nice check.

Fun fact: Galileo is said to have tested falling objects by dropping them from the Leaning Tower of Pisa. Historians aren't sure it ever happened, but the physics is the same as your problem minus the throw.
